node: AC9S8U03 n1
woven: [AC9S7H01, AC9S7I07]
unit: plates
title: What's inside the Earth?
summary: "Earth has layers: a thin solid crust, a thick solid mantle that flows very slowly, a liquid outer core and a solid inner core. Temperature and pressure rise with depth. The lithosphere (crust plus the rigid top of the mantle) is the rigid outer shell that breaks into plates."
language: science
voice: { name: af_heart, speed: 1.1 }
app:
  command: node "$REPO_ROOT/tools/serve.mjs" "$REPO_ROOT/dist/_playground-board" 8230
  url: http://127.0.0.1:8230/index.html
  readySelector: "#gpanel"
  layout: full
explainPicture: { ref: boards.yml#explain, caption: "A wedge of the Earth: crust, mantle, outer core and inner core (outer layers drawn thicker than to scale)." }
explainClip:
  query: { code: "@boards.yml#explain", fresh: 1, id: explain }
  caption: "Earth's layers"
  say: "Crust, mantle, outer core and inner core: hotter and higher pressure with depth."
  clip:
    - caption: { text: "A wedge of the Earth, from the crust to the centre.", say: "A wedge of the Earth, from the crust to the centre." }
    - wait: 3280
    - click: { selector: "#lyd" }
    - expect: { selector: "body", contains: "Outer core" }
    - caption: { text: "About 3,000 km down: the liquid outer core.", say: "About three thousand kilometres down: the liquid outer core." }
    - wait: 4200
    - press: "End"
    - expect: { selector: "body", contains: "Inner core" }
    - caption: { text: "The centre: the solid inner core, hottest and under the most pressure.", say: "At the centre, the inner core is solid: hottest, and under the most pressure." }
    - wait: 600
hook: "The deepest hole ever drilled reached about 12 km. The centre of the Earth is 6371 km down. Everything we know about the rest comes from earthquakes."

Before plates can make sense, you need a picture of what they sit on.

## Engage: solid or liquid?

```step
stage: predict
insight: "Students who picture a molten mantle under the crust can't explain rigid plates; the board shows the mantle is solid rock that flows very slowly."
check:
  type: predict
  q: "Under the crust is the mantle, almost 3000 km thick. What do you predict it is like?"
  options: ["A sea of liquid magma", "Solid rock that is so hot it can flow very slowly", "Hollow", "Ice"]
  actual: "Solid rock, hot enough to flow very slowly over millions of years, like extremely stiff putty. Only small pockets melt into magma. The only liquid layer is the outer core."
```

## Explore: cut a wedge

```step
stage: run
insight: "Clicking each layer and probing temperature and pressure with depth builds the layered model; seeing it to scale shows how thin the crust really is."
try: { playground: board, starter: "boards.yml#wedge", height: 660 }
check: { type: board, text: "Find all six layers and probe down to the centre.", when: "n = k and m >= 6000" }
hint: ["The layers near the surface are thin, so stay on the bigger view and click close to the outer edge of the wedge, one band at a time.", "The line under the board tells you how many layers you've found and how deep you've probed, and the Depth slider takes you all the way down."]
```

Click each layer to find out what it is. Drag the **Depth** slider down to the centre: watch the temperature and pressure. Then press **Show it to scale**.

## Explain: layers and the lithosphere

```step
stage: investigate
insight: "Separating the rigid lithosphere from the soft asthenosphere below is the idea the plate model needs."
tasks:
  - check:
      type: sort
      q: "Solid or liquid?"
      options: ["Solid", "Liquid"]
      items:
        - ["Crust", "Solid"]
        - ["Mantle", "Solid", "Solid, but it flows very slowly over millions of years."]
        - ["Outer core", "Liquid"]
        - ["Inner core", "Solid", "Hotter than the outer core, but the enormous pressure keeps it solid."]
    hint: ["The inner core is the hottest layer, so what else keeps going up as you go deeper, and what might that do to the rock?", "Pressure keeps rising as you go deeper too, so think about what being squeezed that hard does to how closely the particles can pack."]
  - check:
      type: question
      q: "What is the lithosphere?"
      options: ["The crust plus the rigid top of the mantle: Earth's rigid outer shell", "Another name for the crust", "The liquid layer the plates float on", "The core"]
      answer: 0
      feedback: [null, "It includes the top of the mantle as well as the crust.", "The asthenosphere below it is solid but soft, not liquid.", "It's the outermost layer."]
  - check:
      type: question
      q: "What happens to temperature and pressure as you go deeper?"
      options: ["Both increase", "Both decrease", "Temperature increases, pressure stays the same", "They stay the same"]
      answer: 0
      feedback: [null, "Probe deeper on the board.", "The weight of all the rock above presses down harder the deeper you go.", "Probe deeper on the board."]
  - check: { type: reflect, text: "I can name Earth's layers with their states, and explain what the lithosphere is." }
```

## Elaborate: the skin of an apple

```step
stage: modify
tier: typical
insight: "The to-scale view makes the thinness of the crust concrete."
check:
  type: question
  q: "If the Earth were an apple, the crust would be about as thick as the apple's skin. What does that tell you?"
  options: ["The crust is extremely thin compared with the whole Earth", "The crust is the thickest layer", "The Earth is hollow", "The crust is soft"]
  answer: 0
  feedback: [null, "Compare: 35 km of crust against 6371 km to the centre.", "The mantle is thickest.", "It's solid all the way, except the liquid outer core."]
```

## Elaborate: how do we know?

```step
stage: modify
tier: wider
insight: "Reasoning from seismic evidence shows how a model of something unseen is built."
check:
  type: question
  q: "One kind of earthquake wave (S-waves) can't travel through liquids. On the far side of the Earth from a big earthquake, no S-waves arrive. What does that suggest?"
  options: ["Part of the Earth's interior (the outer core) is liquid", "The mantle is liquid", "The waves get tired", "The core is too hot for the waves to pass through"]
  answer: 0
  feedback: [null, "S-waves travel through the mantle, so it must be solid; the liquid layer is deeper down.", "Waves don't tire; they are blocked or bent.", "Heat doesn't stop S-waves: they pass through the hot, solid mantle. A liquid stops them."]
  explain: "This 'S-wave shadow' is how the liquid outer core was discovered."
```

## Evaluate: look back

```step
stage: info
check: { type: reflect, text: "I compared my first answer about the mantle with what I now know." }
```

Write one sentence: "At first I thought… Now I think… because…"

**Revision summary**

- **Crust** (thin, solid) → **mantle** (thick, solid but flows very slowly) → **outer core** (liquid iron and nickel) → **inner core** (solid iron and nickel).
- **Temperature and pressure increase** with depth.
- The **lithosphere** (crust + rigid top of the mantle) is the rigid outer shell, broken into plates; it rests on the soft, slowly flowing **asthenosphere**.

```teacher
summary: Students describe Earth's layers and their states, explain that
  temperature and pressure increase with depth, and identify the lithosphere as
  the rigid outer layer (AC9S8U03, node 1, a hinge node).
time: 20
timing: Engage and Explore 8 min · Explain 7 min · Evaluate 3 min · Typical adds
  1 min, Wider about 2 min
goals:
  - I can name Earth's layers and say whether each is solid or liquid.
  - I can explain that temperature and pressure increase with depth.
  - I can explain that the lithosphere is the rigid outer shell (crust and top
    of the mantle).
before: >
  A concept tutorial for introducing or revising the idea. Set the width with
  `?width=minimum`, `typical` (default) or `wider`.


  The hinge misconception is a liquid mantle ("a sea of magma"). If the mantle
  were liquid, rigid plates wouldn't make sense. The board describes it as solid
  rock that flows very slowly.


  Board notes: the default view enlarges the outer layers so they can be
  clicked; "Show it to scale" draws true thicknesses. Temperatures and pressures
  are rough textbook values joined smoothly (for example, about 1300 °C at the
  base of the lithosphere, about 5400 °C at the centre). Depths: continental
  crust about 35 km (oceanic about 7), lithosphere about 100 km, asthenosphere
  to about 350 km, core–mantle boundary 2890 km, inner core from 5150 km.
running:
  - "Engage: count how many chose the sea of magma."
  - "Explore: ask what surprised them in the to-scale view."
  - "Explain: the lithosphere question is the checkpoint."
struggle: Accepting a solid mantle that still flows. When a student says lava
  comes from a liquid mantle, ask where the board says melting happens.
stuck:
  - see: A student says lava comes from a liquid mantle.
    ask: Where does the board say melting happens?
    fix: "Only in small pockets, where pressure drops or water is added: magma, not
      a whole liquid layer."
  - see: A student thinks the inner core must be liquid because it's hottest.
    ask: What else increases with depth?
    fix: "Pressure: enough to keep it solid."
stretch: Australia sits on very old, stable lithosphere. Why might that mean few
  volcanoes and big earthquakes here?
support: Give a cross-section outline with the layer names and states in a box to place.
leads: >
  Next: what moves the plates (node 2).

  In class: a hard-boiled egg with a cracked shell as a model of the lithosphere
  (and where it breaks down).
exit:
  q: Name the only liquid layer and explain what the lithosphere is.
  a: "The outer core. The lithosphere is the crust plus the rigid top of the
    mantle: the rigid outer shell broken into plates."
explain: >
  **Layers:** crust (thin, solid), mantle (solid, flows very slowly), outer core
  (liquid), inner core (solid). Temperature and pressure rise with depth. The
  **lithosphere** (crust + rigid upper mantle) is the rigid outer shell broken
  into plates; it rests on the soft asthenosphere.
```
